retraction.reason: Retracted in M42 batch 17 under brief §1: the record earns no honest edge. The English article, at revision 1367239958, is eleven kilobytes and argues the convention out of principle 10 of the Rio Declaration — "It is by far the most impressive elaboration of principle 10 of the Rio Declaration, which stresses the need for citizens’ participation in environmental issues" — and forward to nothing at all. The Rio Declaration is not a record here. Its subject is access to environmental information and public participation, which the two environmental records this same batch brings — the Vienna ozone convention and the Montreal protocol it reinstates — have nothing to do with: a protocol on chlorofluorocarbons is not what an information-access convention answered. This is the ninth environmental instrument retracted on arrival and §7.4 of docs/m42-pool.md is the general case: the hole is not that the atlas lacks environmental treaties, it is that it holds no environmental *event* for one to have decided anything about. It waits on a record of the Rio Earth Summit of 1992.
